The outside operator

Four jobs on every round, every shift

Read

Local gauges, sight glasses and indicators.

Look and listen

Machines smooth, traps cycling, flanges tight.

Check the line-up

Every hand valve where the P&ID says.

Compare

Field readings against the DCS, before the shift hands over.

Thirteen stations in one order, door to door

The round is of walking with two climbs; a fixed order means nothing is skipped.

What the operator sees at each station

Every station mixes gauges to read, machines to check and hand valves; the numbers are the design-point readings.

Interactive · station 8 at EL +110.0, seen from the head of the ladder · click an item

The top valve deck: fourteen items on one platform

Grade stations are walked; station 8 is climbed, so plan it with both hands free.

One platform carries the switching valves, bed pressures and relief valves of both adsorbers.

Interactive · elevation view from layout.json · pick a level

Grade and five platforms: know where you will stand

Most items are read at grade; the platforms hold the valves and relief valves that need a climb.

From the station texts of the Visual plant 3D tab

Three hazards decide how you walk the round

O2 service · V-102

No oil, grease or rags; carry a portable O2 detector.

N2-rich gas · V-103

About 12 % O2: never put your head in a vent plume.

Height · PL-1

EL +110.0 by two ladder flights; hold the handrail.

Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • Read, look and listen, check the line-up, compare.
  • Thirteen stations in one fixed order.
  • Gauges, machines and hand valves at every station.
  • Grade plus five platforms; PL-1 is the top deck.
  • O2 service, N2-rich gas and height shape the walk.

Interactive · ISA 5.1 letters on this plant's tags · pick a tag

The letters say what is measured and what the device does

First letter = the variable, next letters = the job, the number = the loop on the P&ID.

One measurement, two displays

The field and the control room should agree

Transmitter

PT-103 sends one signal to PIC-103 and shows it locally.

Field only

The level glass LG-104 and the trap DT-104.

DCS only

Bed thermocouples TE-116/117/118: not read on a round.

A field reading that disagrees with the DCS is reported, never overwritten.

Interactive · gauge lab on the settled design run (model, 1 s samples, two half cycles)

A cycling plant moves the needle every few seconds

One glance gives one point of a swing: watch for a minute and write the range.

Interactive · the rounds-sheet rule of the Visual plant 3D tab, on the design run

The sheet accepts any value the plant reached in the last two minutes

The gauge swings, so the sheet checks a window, not one instant.

Inside the two-minute band plus the reading tolerance is right; a value the plant never reached is refused.

Interactive · the rounds sheet of the Visual plant 3D tab · pick a station

Twenty-eight rows, in the order you walk

Numbers carry a tolerance; states are choices; together they cover the whole round.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • Tag letters: the variable first, then the job.
  • One transmitter feeds the DCS and the local display.
  • Cycling pressures swing; note the range over a minute.
  • The sheet accepts the last two minutes plus a tolerance.
  • Twenty-eight rows in walking order.

Part 3 · Hand valves and line-ups

Which hand valves must be where, and what does one in the wrong position do?

Part 3 · the plan

From the P&ID line-up to the valve in your hand

  1. Normal positionsNO, NC and LO on P&ID rev B
  2. The 32 valveswhat moving each one does
  3. Car sealswhy nine valves are locked open
  4. A valve off normal on the modelfour what-ifs from the design point

PSA-PID-001/002 rev B (P&ID tab)

Every hand valve has a normal position on the drawing

NO ·

Normally open: block and utility isolation valves.

NC ·

Normally closed: vents, drains, sample points, bypasses.

LO ·

Car-sealed open: a numbered wire seal; breaking it needs a permit.

The line-up check compares each valve with this column, station by station.

Interactive · hand-valve table of the Visual plant 3D tab · filter, then pick a valve

What moving each valve does to the plant

solid = NO · dashed = NC · red = LO (car-sealed)

Closing an NO or LO valve, or opening an NC one, changes the process; the normal column is the safe state.

Interactive · the nine LO valves in three groups · pick a group

Car seals guard the valves whose closure does not show at once

Each LO valve removes a flow path or a protection; only a permit with the unit stopped may break the seal.

Interactive · model runs from the design point, valve moved at 1 min, 20 min shown

One hand valve in the wrong position moves the whole unit

The table says what a valve does; the model shows how fast it happens.

The model does what the plant would: pressures move within minutes, and some valves end in a trip.

From the hand-valve table and the station texts

Move a hand valve slowly, and know what it releases

Tell the panel first

The DCS sees the effect; the panel operator must expect it.

Slowly

HV-151/152: never leave both shut on a warm, full shell.

O2 points

HV-182, HV-183, HV-186: O2-clean fittings, no ignition sources.

N2-rich points

HV-191, HV-194, HV-136: oxygen-deficient gas, stand clear.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • 32 hand valves: 10 NO, 13 NC, 9 LO.
  • Each valve's normal position is its safe state.
  • Car seals guard bed blocks, root valves, relief inlets.
  • One valve off normal can trip the unit.
  • Tell the panel, move slowly, mind O2 and N2-rich gas.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Walk the same thirteen stations in the same order every shift.

2

Watch a swinging gauge for a minute and write its range.

3

Report a field reading that disagrees with the DCS.

4

Check every hand valve against its normal position on the P&ID.

5

Never break a car seal without a permit and a stopped unit.
